page.overview:
Who is Bai Yin Du?

Bai Yin was raised in Liyuan by her father, who was born under Fire Nation occupation of the Earth Kingdom during the Hundred Year War. By the time of her youth, the area around her hometown had long suffered under a great drought. Having sustained burn scars across his arms during the old Fire Nation rule, her father's health steadily deteriorated as he grew older. Witnessing his struggles, Bai Yin dedicated herself to strengthening her community so it could endure the drought just as it had survived the war.

When Kya arrived in Liyuan as a voluntary aid worker, Bai Yin welcomed the Avatar's daughter and escorted her to her quarters. Later that week, she invited Kya to dinner, where she introduced her to her father and explained the hardships her community had endured over the decades. Determined to prevent Liyuan from succumbing to the drought, Bai Yin shared her resolve to secure its future.

The next day, Bai Yin and her soldiers defended Liyuan against a raid by sandbending bandits. Although they drove off the attackers, they failed to prevent them from escaping with one of the village's water casks. Frustrated by the outcome, Bai Yin blamed the failure on her soldiers' reliance on sandbending. In response, Tsetseg agreed to help her recruit more benders from across the Si Wong Desert. Bai Yin also enlisted Kya because of her healing abilities. When the waterbender questioned why they could not simply borrow another cask from the military outpost, Bai Yin explained that there was never enough water in the desert and that obtaining more would inevitably deprive another community of its share.

Guided by Anwat and Tsetseg aboard their sand-sailers, Bai Yin and Kya traveled to a hamlet settled by a wayfinding stone. The elder firmly denied that any benders lived there, but Bai Yin was convinced he was lying. Furious, she demanded that he reveal their whereabouts. A young sandbender named Dorzhi ultimately stepped forward and surrendered himself without protest. Bai Yin thanked him for his patronage and assured him that his clan would receive water after one month of his service.
